title: Bookmark Atlas

hero.lead: It saves your GitHub stars and X bookmarks on your own computer and lets you search them: from the terminal, from AI assistants, or from a palette inside the pi coding agent. One person wrote it in about three weeks, and it needs no outside libraries to run.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.sub: One database file in the middle, three ways to ask it questions, and importers that fill it.
sections.plain: Think of a personal library. Your saved repos and posts are the books, the database is the shelf. You can ask the librarian by typing a command, through an AI assistant, or in the pi search palette. Importers fetch new books from GitHub and X.
sections.caption: Hover or tab to a box to highlight what it talks to. The dashed line means the palette reads the database directly, read-only. The palette runs the CLI as a separate process and shares no code with `src/`; a test [ref:test/parity.test.ts] keeps their behaviour in step. [ref:index.ts:315]

sections.title: One request, step by step
sections.sub: What happens when you ask: "Is there anything I saved that fits what I am building?"
sections.plain: The tool does not only search for your words. It also looks at what you are working on right now (git branch, recent changes, the libraries you use) and uses that to pick the best matches.

sections.title: The parts
sections.sub: One file per job. Line counts are under each name.

groups.name: Doors in: how a request or new data arrives

rows.name: src/cli.ts
rows.what: The main switchboard. You type a command, it picks the right helper.
rows.how: One chain of `if` checks over 13 commands.

rows.name: src/mcp.ts
rows.what: Lets AI assistants search your bookmarks. Four tools, all read-only.
rows.how: JSON over standard input and output: search_bookmarks, get_bookmark, suggest_for_task, related_bookmarks.

rows.name: extensions/bookmark-atlas/index.ts
rows.what: The search palette in the pi agent: `/bookmarks` to browse, `/consult` for suggestions.
rows.how: Runs the CLI for refresh, notes, related and recall. Opens the database read-only.

rows.name: src/receiver.ts
rows.what: A tiny web server only your own computer can reach. A browser helper sends saved X posts to it.
rows.how: 127.0.0.1:41009, secret token, accepts x.com and twitter.com, 8 MiB limit.

rows.name: src/search.ts
rows.what: Plain word search. Matches in the title count most.

rows.name: src/recall.ts
rows.what: The clever part. Suggests bookmarks that fit your current project.
rows.how: Reads manifests, merges six ranked lists, filters, adds bonuses. Also finds related items.

rows.name: src/stage.ts
rows.what: Describes what you are working on, using git.
rows.how: Branch, last 12 commits, up to 20 files. No database access.

rows.name: src/github.ts
rows.what: Fetches your starred repositories from GitHub.
rows.how: Token from env or `gh auth token`, 100 per page, ETag for "nothing changed".

rows.name: src/enrich.ts
rows.what: Downloads each repo's README so search can find words inside it.
rows.how: Up to 8 workers (default 4), 25 repos per run, size cap.

rows.name: src/x.ts
rows.what: Understands X bookmark files and stores posts, media and text.
rows.how: Siftly, X API v2 and TweetXVault formats. Skips broken entries.

rows.name: src/collector.ts
rows.what: Runs the separate `tweetxvault` tool, then imports what it exported.

rows.name: src/db.ts
rows.what: Opens the database, creates and upgrades its tables, decides where the file lives.
rows.how: SQLite, write-ahead log, foreign keys, 5 s busy timeout.

sections.title: Where the data lives
sections.sub: One SQLite file: `~/Library/Application Support/bookmark-atlas/bookmarks.db`, about 84 MB.
sections.plain: Every saved item is a "resource". Around it hang the details: when you saved it, your notes, the downloaded text, and for X posts the media. Removing a bookmark deletes nothing at first. The save is only marked as removed, and the `prune` command later cleans up orphans.

cards.text: Downloaded text in passages, plus two search indexes.

sections.note: File location, in order: `BOOKMARK_ATLAS_DB`, then `BOOKMARK_ATLAS_DATA_DIR`, then your user folder. No override is set on this machine. [ref:db.ts:413-428] The search indexes use a stemmer and ignore accents, so "running" finds "run". [ref:db.ts:177]

sections.title: How results are ranked
sections.sub: Two recipes: a plain word search and the project-aware recall.
sections.plain: *Search* splits your words, drops filler like "the" and finds bookmarks containing any of them, with title matches counting most. *Recall* asks the same question six ways (your task, plus context from your project), merges the lists, gives a big bonus to bookmarks that mention a library you use, and throws weak matches out.

panels.title: Search: how much each place counts
panels.note: Scored with bm25, newest save breaks ties, default limit 10, no minimum score. [ref:search.ts:77-142]

panels.title: Recall: the ingredients
rows: Each library you use that the bookmark mentions
panels.note: Six lists merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. A match must cover 35% of the task weight and 30% in total unless a library matches. Only still-saved items count. [ref:recall.ts:31, 60-64, 261, 538-657]

sections.title: What changed most
sections.plain: The docs change more than any code file, which is normal for a young tool. The palette extension is the code file that moves most and also the biggest, so surprises are most likely there. All 64 commits are from one person, and about 70% came in a single week.

weeks.title: Commits per week
weeks.note: Changed together most: README with the extension (19 times), README with `cli.ts` (15), extension with its test (12). On 22 and 23 September a semantic-search stack was removed (commits `a228cda`, `cf9285c`).

sections.title: Things to watch
sections.sub: Nothing here is broken. These are the places where a surprise is most likely.
sections.plain: The most useful finding: `search` and `recall` disagree about bookmarks you removed. After that come a few missing safety nets: no retries when GitHub is slow, and no tests for the main switchboard and the browser receiver.

items.title: Search still shows bookmarks you removed
items.text: A removed bookmark is only marked as removed. `recall` skips it, `search` returns it. The same question gives different answers.
items.tech: [ref:recall.ts:234, 261, 280, 426] filter removed saves. In [ref:search.ts:125] the marker only changes the date shown. [read] and confirmed by a second reviewer.

items.title: GitHub sync stops at the first hiccup
items.text: If GitHub says "slow down" or the network drops once, the sync stops and you start it again. The tool never waits and retries.
items.tech: Any non-OK answer throws. No retry or rate-limit handling in `github.ts`, `enrich.ts`, `collector.ts`. [ref:github.ts:270-271] [read]

items.title: The switchboard and the browser receiver have no tests of their own
items.text: No test loads `cli.ts`, `collector.ts`, `receiver.ts` or `stage.ts` directly. The receiver is the only part that listens on a network port. Indirect coverage is unknown.

items.title: The database has no version number
items.text: Each time it opens, the database checks what is missing and fixes it. That works, but nothing records which upgrades ran, and some rebuild the search index on open.

items.title: One 1334-line file holds the palette, and one function exists twice
items.text: The data-folder function is copied into the extension on purpose, because a symlinked extension cannot import shared code. A test fails if the copies drift apart.

items.title: Your X login lives in another tool, and AI clients can read your bookmark text
items.text: `tweetxvault` handles X access, and we could not see where it stores your session. Any AI you connect through MCP can read bookmark text; the tool tells it to treat that text as untrusted.
items.tech: [ref:collector.ts:42-56] [ref:mcp.ts:127-141] [read] for both facts, [guess] for where the data goes next.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.sub: Commands come from `package.json`. We did not run them.
sections.plain: You need Node.js 24 or newer. From a checkout, use `node src/cli.ts` instead of the installed command. The only secret you must set is the token for the browser receiver. GitHub access reuses your `gh` login if no token is set.
sections.code:
# from a checkout                          # settings (environment variables)
node src/cli.ts status                     BOOKMARK_ATLAS_DB, BOOKMARK_ATLAS_DATA_DIR   where the database lives
npm test            # node --test          BOOKMARK_ATLAS_GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN      else: gh auth token
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit         BOOKMARK_ATLAS_X_CAPTURE_TOKEN               needed for "capture x"
npm run build       # writes dist/         BOOKMARK_ATLAS_TWEETXVAULT_BIN, _DIR         the tweetxvault tool

# installed package
bookmark-atlas recall "task" --repo "$PWD"
sections.note: CI runs type check and tests on Ubuntu and macOS, then checks the package contents. A tag starting with `v` publishes to npm. [ref:ci.yml] [ref:release.yml]

sections.title: Words you will see
items: Resource
One saved item: a GitHub repo or an X post.
Save
The link between you and a resource. Removing it only marks it.
Capture, chunk
Downloaded text of a resource, and the passages it is cut into.
Recall, consult
Ask for saved items that fit your task and project.
Stage
A short description of your current work, built from git.
MCP
Model Context Protocol, a standard for AI assistants to call tools.
pi
The coding agent that hosts the palette extension.
TweetXVault
A separate tool that downloads your X bookmarks.
FTS5
SQLite's built-in word search.
bm25
A standard formula that scores how well a text matches your words.
Rank fusion (RRF)
A way to merge several ranked lists into one fair list.
ETag
A stamp that lets GitHub answer "nothing changed".
Provenance
A signed npm record showing which build made a package.
